title: System Sentinel — Induction
description: One-time induction that adapts the System Sentinel to the user's machine: verifies the platform and tools, runs a read-only inventory, sets warning thresholds, writes the local adaptation layer, and confirms readiness.

constraints: - You MUST run scripts/inventory.sh and confirm the detected OS family is linux or macos
- You MUST report the privilege level, since it determines which fields will be collectable
- You MUST NOT proceed silently if the platform is unsupported — say so and stop
rail.validation: Report the detected OS family, version and privilege level, and confirm support.

constraints: - You MUST verify bash and python3 are available
- You MUST verify the coreutils used by the inventory are present (df, uptime, uname)
- You MUST NOT install anything without user confirmation
rail.validation: Report which required tools are present and which are missing, with install commands for the detected package manager.

constraints: - You MUST present the default warning thresholds from sops/system-assessment.sop.md
- You SHOULD ask whether the user wants to tighten any threshold
- You MUST record the chosen thresholds in the local adaptation layer
rail.validation: Confirm the thresholds to be used for this machine.

constraints: - You MUST create local/environment.yaml with detected OS, privilege level, report format preference and thresholds
- You MUST NOT include credentials or secrets
- You MUST NOT modify any curated-core file (scripts/, taskrails/, sops/, schemas/, SYSTEM.md, agent.yaml)
rail.validation: Confirm local/environment.yaml was created and that no curated file changed.

constraints: - You MUST run tests/readiness-check.sh and report PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL
- You MUST tell the user the command to start an assessment: the 'system-assessment' taskrail
- You MUST NOT start an assessment automatically
rail.validation: Confirm readiness status and hand off to the system-assessment taskrail.
